title: Neighborhood music as a boy
summary: Photograph of the Magnolia band with Oliver; as a child he heard two white bands and shined shoes in the district, then moved to Conti area.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That's Jew Oliver in that time when I was the manager of the band.

Now, is there any other subject I would like to... I was wondering anything else about your neighborhood when you were a kid. Do you remember any parades up there or any other dance halls or anything around the neighborhood when you were very small?

Well, I was very small. What kind of music you heard when you were a little kid? Well, when I was small, I used to hear them. They had two white bands right across from me. And that was on Custom House Street between Fred and Johnson. And I was shining shoes at the proper time in the district. And Freddie was also shining shoes. That was pretty close to the district where you lived then, wasn't it? Well, then I moved from Iverville, from Custom House Street to Viro. And that was 427, not Viro Street. That was between St. Louis and Conti. But near St. Louis. About how old were you? I must have been about, say, about 12 years old then.
